topic: The noisy-GHZ optimized-witness equality question in Xu et al., arXiv:2211.05563v1, Section 4.2, page 12
title: A strict gap in the noisy-GHZ equality question of Xu et al., Section 4.2, page 12 of arXiv:2211.05563v1

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: The question in Xu et al., Section 4.2, page 12 of arXiv:2211.05563v1, asks whether the optimized witness bound equals the convex-roof geometric measure of genuine multipartite entanglement for noisy GHZ states. A strict separation holds for every party count n >= 3 and local dimension d >= 3 at an explicit noise probability. For three qutrits at noise p=3/8, the optimized witness bound is exactly 1/9, whereas the convex roof is at least 13/108. A biseparable overlap inequality and a positive-definite matrix give a two-observable lower bound. A written corollary extends the three-qutrit strict gap throughout 27/74 < p < 9/22.
summary: A strict gap holds at an explicit noise probability for every n,d >= 3. At n=d=3 and p=3/8, epsilon=1/9 < 13/108 <= E_G; strict separation also holds for 27/74 < p < 9/22. The pinned Lean declaration refutes universal equality through the base-case inequalities; the exact optimized value, generalization and interval are written proofs, supplemented by exact finite arithmetic checks.
